description:
Write cached lens output into the EXIF/IPTC/XMP metadata blocks of an enriched copy of the photo. The original is never written: the copy comes back as base64, or is saved to a new `outputPath`. The photo must have been analyzed before (analyze_photo or analyze_batch). Never overwrites an existing file unless you pass `overwrite: true`, and never writes over the input file.

The enriched photo carries its structured intelligence in standard metadata fields any downstream tool can read. No Phototology API call is needed to access the analysis after enrichment. Useful when handing a photo off to another app or archiving it.

Cost: 5 credits per call. Bills regardless of cache state; writing the enriched copy is its own billable operation.

For local files, the optional `outputPath` parameter saves the enriched copy to that new path so you don't have to handle the base64 yourself. Without it, the tool returns the enriched bytes as `imageBase64`. Base64 input over about 150 KB is discouraged; pass `imageUrl` or `imagePath` instead.

Returns `{ mode, savedTo?, sidecarSavedTo?, imageBase64?, sidecar?, formatsWritten, lensVersions, sha256, registryId?, credentials?, reason?, note?, usage: { creditsCharged, usd: { charged } }, warnings?, meta?, resolvedPath? }`. `mode` is `file` when the metadata went into the image bytes, or `sidecar` when the API left the file untouched and returned an XMP packet instead (`reason` says why): `sidecarSavedTo` names the `.xmp` file it was saved to, otherwise the packet is in `sidecar.xmp`. `credentials` is what the API read from the input photo's content credential, before the write; with `breakCredentials: true` the written copy no longer carries a valid content credential, even when `credentials` reports one. `note` says in plain words why the photo was left untouched, or what a copy lost. `usage.creditsCharged` is the credits this call spent and `usage.usd.charged` its dollar value (e.g. "0.05"). `warnings` carries the API's `CREDENTIAL_INVALIDATED` or `CREDENTIALS_UNREAD`, and a line when the preview could not be made. `meta` is the API's request metadata (request id, timing). `resolvedPath` is present only when a symlinked folder led to a different file than the one named.

When the result has image bytes, it also carries an `image` content block: a JPEG preview of the enriched photo, longest edge at most 1024 px, so you can see the photo without loading the full-resolution bytes.

If the photo carries a valid content credential, writing the analysis into the file would break its content credential, so the tool leaves the photo untouched and returns the analysis as an XMP sidecar instead. With `imagePath`, the sidecar is saved beside the original as `<imagePath>.xmp` (same overwrite rules as `outputPath`); otherwise it comes back as `sidecar.xmp`. Pass `breakCredentials: true` to write the copy anyway. Billed the same either way.

If the photo has not been analyzed before, returns a PHOTO_NOT_IN_REGISTRY error. Call `analyze_photo` first, then `enrich_photo`.

breakCredentials.description: Write the enriched copy even when the photo carries a valid content credential. Pass true only if the user accepts that the written copy loses its content credential. By default the analysis goes into a sidecar file next to the photo and the photo is left untouched. When true, the result warns CREDENTIAL_INVALIDATED.

formats.description: Which metadata blocks to write. Defaults to ["xmp"], the smallest and most portable. Use ["exif", "iptc", "xmp"] to write all three. c2pa signing is deferred to a future release.

imageBase64.description: Base64-encoded image bytes (no data: URL prefix). Keep it under about 150 KB; for larger files prefer imageUrl or imagePath.

imagePath.description: Absolute local-filesystem path on the machine running the MCP server. The MCP reads the file and forwards bytes. Accepts absolute (/Users/...) or ~/-prefixed paths.

imageUrl.description: Publicly fetchable image URL. Server fetches, computes sha256, looks up the registry, writes the enriched bytes, and returns them as base64.

outputPath.description: Optional absolute local-filesystem path where the enriched copy is saved. Accepts absolute or ~/-prefixed paths. When provided, the tool writes the enriched bytes to this path and returns savedTo instead of imageBase64, so agents can enrich a local file without handling base64 themselves. This is always a new file: the original photo is never written. When omitted, the response carries the enriched bytes as imageBase64. Refuses an existing file unless overwrite is true, and always refuses the input file itself.

overwrite.description: Allow outputPath, or the <imagePath>.xmp sidecar, to replace an existing file. Defaults to false. Never permits writing over the input file (imagePath), even when true.

name: enrich_photo
title: Write analysis into a copy of the photo
